params_history.analysis: 83.3% win rate with avg RR of 1.11 across 6 trades suggests the zone scoring is solid but actual RR achieved (1.11) is far below the default_rr_ratio (2.5), indicating targets are likely being manually adjusted or the min_rr_ratio is being used. All winning trades had RR between 1.44-1.72, well below the 2.0 min_rr_ratio setting, suggesting the min_rr_ratio param is not being enforced or zones are being entered with tighter targets. The single loss occurred in a volatile regime with a high-scoring zone (52/60), indicating volatile conditions may need wider stops.

Win rate of 42.9% with avg RR of 0.05 indicates the strategy is barely breaking even. Winning trades averaged score 48.7/60 and achieved RR 1.72 avg, while losing trades averaged score 48.5/60 with full SL hits. BUY trades in trending_up regime went 1W/3L (25% WR) which is counterintuitive, while SELL trades in ranging regime went 2W/1L (67% WR).

Only 2 trades in 10 days with a 50% win rate and net P&L of ₹3. The winning trade scored 47/60 while the losing trade scored 41/60, suggesting a higher min_score threshold around 45 could have filtered the loss. Both trades were SELL-side; the winner paradoxically occurred in a trending_up regime (counter-trend) while the loser failed in trending_down (with-trend), indicating regime alignment alone isn't predictive with this small sample.

All 3 trades were SELL-side with scores 46-48/60 and all lost, yielding 0% win rate and avg RR of -0.97. Two SL_HIT trades occurred in trending_up and ranging regimes where sell pressure was insufficient, suggesting a critical regime-alignment issue. The current 1.0x ATR stop is too tight given adverse moves of 1.18-1.32 RR against, and the 3.0 default RR target appears too ambitious for zones that cannot hold.

All 4 trades resulted in losses with 0% win rate and avg RR of -1.00. The lowest score trade (HINDUNILVR at 35/60) produced the largest loss (₹-24), while even higher-scored zones (50-52/60) failed, suggesting the SL is too tight at 1.0 ATR causing premature stops. Average zone score of 45.8 is reasonable but the consistent -1.2x RR losses indicate price is reversing just past the stop level before potentially moving in the intended direction.

final_summary.executive_summary: The walk-forward simulation revealed a sharp performance degradation after the initial 2 weeks (80-100% WR) dropping to near 0% in weeks 7-10, resulting in an overall 43.5% win rate and breakeven avg RR. The 1.0x ATR stop-loss was consistently too tight, with price reversing just past the stop before moving in the intended direction. Parameters never converged—the optimizer oscillated between tight filters (score 50) and loose filters (score 35)—indicating the strategy needs structural improvements beyond parameter tuning, particularly in regime-aware stop placement and trade direction filtering.
key_insights: Stop-loss at 1.0x ATR is systematically too tight: repeated analysis showed losses clustering at exactly -1.0 to -1.25 RR, suggesting price probes past the zone boundary before reversing, requiring at minimum 1.5x ATR stops to survive normal zone retests

Early success (weeks 1-2, 80%+ WR) occurred in what appears to be a trending market favorable to the strategy, while later weeks saw regime shifts that destroyed edge—regime alignment scoring alone (the Trend dimension) was insufficient to prevent counter-trend losses

Higher score thresholds (45-50) reduced trade frequency but did NOT improve win rate in adverse conditions—even 50-52/60 scored zones produced losses, indicating zone quality scoring cannot compensate for poor market timing or inadequate stop width

The SELL-side bias was problematic: most losses came from short trades in trending_up or ranging regimes, suggesting the strategy needs explicit directional filtering beyond the existing trend dimension score
A default RR target of 3.0 was too ambitious and rarely hit; the single best profitable period used 2.5 RR, while winning trades averaged approximately 1.0-1.5 actual RR achieved
final_summary.best_performing_setup: Weeks 1-2 produced 6 trades with 83% win rate and +₹88 P&L using moderate parameters (min_score 35, RR 2.5, SL 1.0 ATR). The common pattern was fresh zones with tight bases (≤3 candles) scored 40+ in clearly trending markets where trade direction aligned with the dominant trend. The single best trade scored 47/60 and captured 1.52R profit, suggesting zones scoring 45+ in strongly trending environments with first-touch (fresh) status represent the highest probability setup.
final_summary.recommended_live_approach: Deploy with conservative parameters emphasizing survival over frequency: use wider stops (1.5x ATR) to avoid premature stop-outs, moderate RR targets (2.0-2.5) that are actually achievable, and a high score threshold (45+) to ensure only institutional-quality zones are traded. Critically, add a hard rule to ONLY trade in the direction of the higher-timeframe trend—no counter-trend zone trades regardless of score. Start with minimum position sizing and require 20+ trades before adjusting parameters. Monitor the stop-hunt pattern closely: if price consistently reverses within 0.5 ATR past the stop level, the zone thesis is correct but execution needs refinement via wider stops or limit orders deeper in the zone.
